sections.label: Code of Conduct for Ministers
sections.summary: The Code of Conduct for Ministers, in force since 1954 and revised in 2005, bars Ministers from directing civil servants to act against Civil Service core values.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Ministers and Members of this House are well aware that our conduct must always be above board.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: There is a Code of Conduct for Ministers which has been in force since 1954.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: It was last revised and laid before this House in 2005.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Code clearly states that a Minister must not direct or request a civil servant to do anything or perform any function that may conflict with the Civil Service's core values of incorruptibility, impartiality, integrity and honesty.

sections.label: Ministerial Committee and Cabinet decisions
sections.summary: The Ministerial Committee told Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling that neither the Committee nor the Cabinet would make any decision.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Ministerial Committee has made it clear to Mr Lee Hsien Yang and, in particular, to Dr Lee Wei Ling, that neither the Ministerial Committee nor the Cabinet will be making any decision.

sections.label: Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong recusal
sections.summary: After Mr Lee Kuan Yew's death, Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong told Cabinet on 15 April 2015 he would recuse himself from Government decisions on the house.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Following the passing of Mr Lee Kuan Yew on 23 March 2015, Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong informed Cabinet on 15 April 2015 that he would recuse himself from all Government decisions to be taken on the house.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: This is in accordance with the guidelines in paragraphs (3) and (4) of the code of conduct for Ministers.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: It was proper for the Prime Minister to recuse himself as there is a conflict of interest between his public role as the Head of Government, and his private role as a son of Mr Lee, and, in addition, because he had been bequeathed the property.

sections.label: Cabinet approves Ministerial Committee
sections.summary: On 1 June 2016, at a Cabinet meeting he chaired, Cabinet approved the Minister for National Development's proposal to set up a Ministerial Committee on 38 Oxley Road options.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: On 1 June 2016, at a Cabinet meeting which I chaired, Cabinet approved the proposal by the Minister for National Development to set up a Ministerial Committee to draw up the range of possible options for 38 Oxley Road.

sections.label: Ministerial Committee terms of reference
sections.summary: The Committee's terms of reference cover the property's heritage significance, Mr Lee Kuan Yew's wishes, and possible plans; his three children were informed in writing on 27 July 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Terms of Reference of this Committee are to assess (a) the historical and heritage significance of the property; (b) the wishes of Mr Lee Kuan Yew in relation to the property; and (c) the possible plans for the property and the neighbourhood and the options to move forward.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: As we wanted to get the views of Mr Lee's children, Mr Lee Hsien Loong, Dr Lee Wei Ling and Mr Lee Hsien Yang were duly informed separately, in writing, on 27 July 2016, that a Ministerial Committee, of which I was the Chairman, had been formed to consider the options for 38 Oxley Road and the implications thereof, and that the Committee would look into various aspects, including what Mr Lee Kuan Yew's thinking on the matter was.

sections.label: Gazetted national monuments
sections.summary: Currently 72 buildings and structures are gazetted as national monuments, some of which were private residences.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Currently, 72 buildings and structures are gazetted as national monuments, some of which were private residences.

sections.label: Public interests at 38 Oxley Road
sections.summary: The Minister for National Development will elaborate later, and these public interests and considerations apply to 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Minister for National Development will elaborate on this later in his speech.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: These public interests and considerations apply to 38 Oxley Road as well.

sections.label: Avoiding irreversible steps on site
sections.summary: Since no decision is needed now, it may be best to avoid irreversible steps like demolition and redevelopment to consider options with historical perspective.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Since we do not need to decide now how best to maintain this important historical link to the past, it might be best, for the time being, to avoid taking irreversible steps, such as demolition and redevelopment of the site, so that we have the benefit of time to consider the matter and the merits of various options with the perspective of history.

sections.label: Lee's 2011 Cabinet meeting wish
sections.summary: At a July 2011 Cabinet meeting, Mr Lee expressed his wish for the house to be demolished but listened to Cabinet members' views.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: When Mr Lee met the Cabinet in July 2011, he expressed his wish for the house to be demolished, but Mr Lee also listened carefully to the views of the Cabinet members.

sections.label: Lee's letter after reflection
sections.summary: Five months later, Mr Lee wrote to the Cabinet informing them he had reflected on the matter.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Mr Lee wrote to the Cabinet five months later, informing us that he had reflected on the matter.

sections.label: Committee invites Lee children's views
sections.summary: The Ministerial Committee wrote to all of Mr Lee's children on 27 July 2016 inviting views on his thinking and its context.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Ministerial Committee wrote to all of Mr Lee's children on 27 July 2016, shortly after the Committee was formed, to invite them to share with the Committee, any views they would like on Mr Lee's thinking on the property, and the context and circumstances relating to his thinking beyond what had already been stated in public, so that these could be taken into account.

sections.label: Lee Hsien Yang's inaccurate account
sections.summary: Mr Lee Hsien Yang's 2 July 2017 statement gives a selective and inaccurate account of his exchanges with the Ministerial Committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Mr Lee Hsien Yang's statement on 2 July 2017 presents a selective and inaccurate account of his exchanges with the Ministerial Committee on 38 Oxley Road house. "Selective" and "inaccurate".

sections.label: No decision on house
sections.summary: The Government would not decide on the house while Dr Lee Wei Ling lives there, and the Committee cannot rule on the last will's validity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The Government had no intention of making any decision on the house, as long as Dr Lee Wei Ling resides there, and Mr Lee Hsien Yang had acknowledged this in one of his subsequent replies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: As such, it was clear to all parties involved that the Government was not making an immediate decision on the house, and that no decision may be necessary for another 20 to 30 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The Committee has no power to decide on the validity of the last will.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: This, too, was made clear to Mr Lee Hsien Yang on 25 April 2017 that the Committee is not the place where decisions on the legal validity of the last will can be made, and this is a matter between him and Mr Lee Hsien Loong.

sections.label: Statutory declarations not required
sections.summary: Mr Lee Hsien Loong gave three statutory declarations, but parties need not respond or submit statutory declarations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Mr Lee Hsien Loong provided his representations in the form of three statutory declarations, but there was no need for any party to respond if they did not wish to provide views or clarifications, and no need for them to put their views down as statutory declarations either.

sections.label: Representations circulated between parties
sections.summary: Both parties made representations to the Committee, and each party's views were circulated to the other with permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Both parties made representations to the Committee that might have been uncomfortable to the other.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Each party's views were circulated, with their permission, to the other party.

sections.label: PM Lee recused himself
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee recused himself and let the Cabinet, chaired by the speaker, decide how to proceed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Instead, Prime Minister Lee did the proper thing, recused himself and let the Cabinet, without him, chaired by me, decide on how to proceed with the matter.

sections.label: Dr Lee Wei Ling's right
sections.summary: The Government said it will not affect Dr Lee Wei Ling's right to live at 38 Oxley Road, and due process should begin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The Government had stated on several occasions that it will not do anything to affect Dr Lee Wei Ling's right to continue living at 38 Oxley Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Even though no decision is needed now, it is prudent to commence that due process which is needed to consider the various options before making any decision on the house, as with all properties of significant public interest.

sections.label: Committee prepares options
sections.summary: The Committee studies and prepares options for the property and neighbourhood so a future government can decide, considering Mr Lee's views.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Instead, the Committee's approach is to study and prepare a range of options for the property and the neighbourhood so that a future government can make an informed and considered decision when it becomes necessary, always taking into account Mr Lee's views.

sections.label: Meeting on property options
sections.summary: At a 27 April 2015 meeting, the speaker told Mr Lee Hsien Yang he would not support the options at either end of the range.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: In our meeting on 27 April 2015, we talked about various possibilities for the property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I informed Mr Lee Hsien Yang that I would personally not support the options at either end of the range.

sections.label: Committee studies intermediate options
sections.summary: The Committee has been studying intermediate options, such as demolishing the house but keeping the basement dining room with a heritage centre attached.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The Committee has been studying various intermediate options, such as demolishing the house but keeping the basement dining room with an appropriate heritage centre attached.

sections.label: Public issues and Government honesty
sections.summary: The speaker urges Members to leave room for private family issues while dealing decisively with public issues, asking probing questions and keeping public institutions neutral.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Even as we do so, I hope that Members will leave enough room for the private issues to be worked through within the family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: But we must not shy away from dealing decisively with the public issues which go to the heart of our system of clean and honest Government, and we must do so for the good of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I urge Members to ask me and my Cabinet colleagues probing questions on any aspect of these allegations which Members feel is relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We must keep our public institutions neutral and not have allegations hurled at our public officers without basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: At the end of this session, Singaporeans should have their confidence in the honesty of our Government and our public officers strengthened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We make decisions and act in the public interest of Singaporeans.
